parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Activate a policy version to a CANARY scope (a subset of the fleet) rather
than fleet-wide. The version is served only to in-scope nodes/tenants (or a
percentage slice) while a metric-based evaluator watches the success window;
it then either promotes fleet-wide, auto-rolls back on breach, or pauses on
an inconclusive signal. Additive to the Phase-K activation surface.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
`GetNativeAccess` runs the same `Authorize` decision and, when allowed,
mints a short-lived contract for the caller to talk to the backend
directly: a restricted role, a scoped DSN, and the exact set of
`app.current_*` session variables the SDK must `SET LOCAL` so the
broker-generated RLS policies still apply. UDB stays the source of the
authorization decision; the native grant only carries it forward.

parameters.name: resourceType
parameters.description:
Optional resource-type filter (UNSPECIFIED == all types).

 - RESOURCE_TYPE_ROUTING_POLICY: Request routing / backend selection policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_METHOD_SECURITY_POLICY: Per-RPC method-security policy (the proto endpoint_security map).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RLS_TENANT_POLICY: Row-level-security / tenant isolation policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_NATIVE_SERVICE_ENABLEMENT: Which native control-plane services are enabled on a node.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_BACKEND_TARGET_DEFINITION: Backend target/cluster definitions — the "definitions" that routing and
RLS policies reference. Pushed BEFORE the referencing policies.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

auto-rolls it back.

v1CanaryState.description:
Lifecycle state of a progressive-rollout canary.

 - CANARY_STATE_PROMOTED: The success window passed within threshold and the canary was promoted
fleet-wide (the version is now the active version of its policy set).
 - CANARY_STATE_ROLLED_BACK: A metric breach inside the window triggered an automatic rollback to the
policy set's prior (rollback) version.
 - CANARY_STATE_PAUSED: The signal was inconclusive (insufficient samples): the canary is held —
neither promoted nor rolled back — pending more data / operator action.

`GetPolicyBundle` serializes the live authorization snapshot (policies,
role bindings, relationship tuples) and signs it so an SDK can cache it
and answer `can()` locally without a round-trip, while still being able
to verify the bundle was issued by UDB and has not expired.

scopeValues.description:
For NODE/TENANT: the list of in-scope ids. For PERCENT: a single-element
list whose value is the integer percentage (1..=100).

successWindowSecs.description: The evaluator waits at least this long before declaring success.

metricThreshold.description:
The success metric breach threshold (e.g. fractional authz deny/error rate).
A measured value strictly greater than this inside the window auto-rolls back.

minSamples.description:
Minimum sample count required for a conclusive evaluation. Below this the
canary PAUSES instead of promoting or rolling back.

rollbackVersionId.description:
The version a rollback restores to (the policy set's active version at
canary-creation time). Recorded so auto-rollback is deterministic.

outcomeReason.description: Why the canary left ACTIVE (breach reason, 'promoted', 'inconclusive').

v1PolicyCanary.description:
A progressive-rollout canary: a `PolicyVersion` exposed to a SUBSET of the
fleet (by node id, tenant id, or percentage) and watched by a metric-based
evaluator before fleet-wide promotion. If the success metric breaches
`metric_threshold` within `success_window_secs`, the canary auto-rolls back
to the policy set's prior version BEFORE fleet-wide impact; if the window
passes within threshold it becomes promote-eligible; if samples are
insufficient it pauses. Every state transition is audited.

v1PolicyDocument.description:
A candidate policy document the governance APIs operate on (drafts and
simulations). Unifies the full field richness of CreatePolicyRule and
PutAuthzPolicy (role, purpose, relationship, priority, required scopes,
conditions, tenant, project, domain) so every governed surface is parity.

v1PolicyDraft.description:
An editable, in-progress policy change set under review (Phase K draft/approval
workflow). Holds the proposed policies/tuples as JSON; when approved it is
promoted into an immutable numbered PolicyVersion. Drafts never affect live
decisions.

⚠️ CROSS-SESSION: field set reconstructed to EXACTLY match the governance
session's `governance_store.rs::load_draft` struct literal (the source of
truth). The governance-session owner should still confirm this is their
intended schema / restore their canonical file.

document.description: Document parsed back from the stored draft (convenience).

v1PolicyRule.description: Managed permission rule mapped into UDB authorization policy rows.

v1PolicySet.description:
A governed collection of policy versions. Each tenant/project/name names one
policy set; its `active_version_id` points at the currently-enforced
`PolicyVersion`, and `rollback_version_id` records the version a rollback
restored to. Drafts are created against a policy set and only take effect
once a version is activated (Phase K governance workflow).

sourceDraftId.description: The PolicyDraft this version was promoted from, if any.

v1PolicyVersion.description:
An immutable, numbered version of a policy set. A `PolicyDraft` that passes
review is promoted into a `PolicyVersion` whose frozen `payload_json`
(policies + role bindings + relationship tuples) is what
`ActivatePolicyVersion` loads into the live authorization snapshot. Drafts
remain editable; versions never change once created — they only transition
state (draft -> pending_review -> approved -> active -> superseded /
rejected / rolled_back). `revision` provides optimistic concurrency over the
version's state transitions; `content_hash` detects no-op promotions.

v1PolicyVersionState.description: Lifecycle state of a governed policy version (Phase K draft/approval workflow).

mappedPrincipalJson.description: Fully-resolved principal fields as JSON for inspection.

roles.description: Roles granted (only roles explicitly present in the mapping).

unmappedGroups.description: Input groups that matched no mapping entry (granted nothing).

v1PromoteCanaryRequest.description:
Promote a baked (within-threshold) canary to fleet-wide. Fails unless the
canary is promote-eligible (ACTIVE and its success window has elapsed within
threshold). On success the canaried version becomes the active version of its
policy set fleet-wide and the canary moves to PROMOTED.

v1Resource.description: One versioned resource on the wire (a single ControlPlaneResource projection).

v1ResourceType.description:
- RESOURCE_TYPE_ROUTING_POLICY: Request routing / backend selection policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_METHOD_SECURITY_POLICY: Per-RPC method-security policy (the proto endpoint_security map).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RLS_TENANT_POLICY: Row-level-security / tenant isolation policy (references backend targets).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_NATIVE_SERVICE_ENABLEMENT: Which native control-plane services are enabled on a node.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_BACKEND_TARGET_DEFINITION: Backend target/cluster definitions — the "definitions" that routing and
RLS policies reference. Pushed BEFORE the referencing policies.
v1ResourceType.title:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ResourceType — the kinds of control-plane configuration a node can subscribe
to in the xDS-style versioned distribution stream. "Definition" resources
(backend targets) MUST be pushed before referencing policies so a referencing
policy is never applied before its target exists (make-before-break).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

backupId.description: The backup run id to restore (resolved to its object prefix).

allowCrossTenant.description:
When the target differs from the source this must be set: a cross-tenant

queryText.description:

The aggregate world version after re-publishing (content-addressed, so it

resourcesRestored.description: Number of resources re-published from the retained snapshot.

plainKey.description: New plain key returned ONCE; the prior secret is invalidated immediately.

roles.title: roles granted via configured group mapping

signatureVerified.description:

v1ScheduleType.description:
How a scheduled job's next fire time is derived.

 - SCHEDULE_TYPE_CRON: Recurring job; next_fire_at is advanced from the cron expression after each fire.
 - SCHEDULE_TYPE_ONE_SHOT: One-shot job; fires exactly once at next_fire_at, then transitions to COMPLETED.

cronExpression.description:
Cron expression for SCHEDULE_TYPE_CRON jobs (ignored for one-shot).

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:cron_expression"

targetTopic.description:
Informational topic the firing consumer is expected to listen on.

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:target_topic"

nextFireAt.description:
When the job is next eligible to fire. NULL once a one-shot job COMPLETED.

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:next_fire_at"

maxAttempts.description:
Maximum delivery attempts before the job is dead-lettered.

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:max_attempts;not null"

attemptCount.description:
Failed attempts since the last successful fire; reset to 0 on success.

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:attempt_count;not null"

backoffSeconds.description:
Base backoff (seconds) used to defer next_fire_at after a failed attempt.

@inject_tag: gorm:"column:backoff_seconds;not null"

v1ScheduledJob.description:
ScheduledJob — a durable cron or one-shot job. The leader-elected scheduler
tick claims DUE rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and FIRES an outbox event
(`udb.scheduler.job.fired.v1`); it never executes the payload in-process —
consumers do the work (at-least-once). After `max_attempts` failures a job is
routed to the dead-letter topic (`udb.scheduler.job.dead.v1`) and marked DEAD.

grantedRoles.description:
Roles granted/revoked as a result of group membership changes (only via
configured group→role mappings).

v1ScimPatchOp.description: SCIM PATCH operations (RFC 7644 §3.5.2): add/replace/remove on a path.

A SCIM resource carried as its canonical JSON body. CRUD handlers persist

v1SearchMode.description:
Query mode for a Search request.

 - SEARCH_MODE_TEXT: Lexical full-text only (requires query_text).
 - SEARCH_MODE_VECTOR: Dense-vector nearest-neighbour only (requires query_vector).
 - SEARCH_MODE_HYBRID: Hybrid lexical + vector fused with reciprocal-rank fusion.

v1Session.description:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Session — Authenticated session for a user, service account, workload, or
external identity mapped into UDB.

Hybrid model:
  SERVER_SIDE: cookie-based; session_token_lookup (keyed HMAC) → hash verify
  JWT:         access_token_jti + refresh_token_jti tracked for revocation

Migration order 2. RLS scopes rows to the current tenant.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

v1WebhookDelivery.title:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WebhookDelivery — the durable, tenant-scoped delivery journal (master-plan
9.4). One row per delivery attempt-run of one event to one endpoint: it
records the outcome (PENDING | DELIVERED | FAILED | DEAD), the attempt count,
the last HTTP response status / error, and the `X-Udb-Signature` that was
sent, so an operator can audit exactly what was delivered where and why a
delivery dead-lettered. RLS scopes rows to the current tenant.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

url.description:
The external HTTPS delivery target. Validated by the SSRF guard at WRITE
time and again (DNS rebinding) at DELIVERY time: https-only, never a host
resolving to a private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT range.

topicPattern.description:
Topic subscription pattern (`*`, `udb.*`, or an exact topic). Selects which
topics reach this endpoint; delivery is still tenant-bound to `tenant_id`.

signingSecret.description:
Per-endpoint HMAC signing secret. STORAGE_ONLY: never surfaced by the
generated read/redaction layer (returned once at creation, like an API key).

active.description: When false the endpoint is paused: no events are delivered to it.

maxAttempts.description:
Maximum delivery attempts before a delivery is dead-lettered
(`udb.webhook.delivery.dead.v1`) and journaled DEAD.

v1WebhookEndpoint.title:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WebhookEndpoint — a per-tenant external HTTP delivery target (master-plan
9.4). The broker delivers tenant-scoped domain events (CDC/outbox) to the
outside world by POSTing the event body to `url`, signed with the
per-endpoint `signing_secret` (HMAC-SHA256 → `X-Udb-Signature`). The
subscription `topic_pattern` selects which topics this endpoint receives, but
delivery is ALWAYS bound to this row's `tenant_id` (never pattern-only): an
event is delivered only when its payload tenant matches `tenant_id`, so a
tenant can never subscribe to another tenant's events. RLS scopes rows to the
current tenant. The signing secret is OUTPUT_VIEW_STORAGE_ONLY — it is
returned exactly once at creation and never surfaced by the read layer again.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

workflowType.description:
Application-defined workflow type (the workflow/saga_kind discriminator). The
engine maps every instance to `saga::SagaKind::Workflow` so the recorded saga
row is distinguishable from a plain data-plane saga; the DEFAULT kind is the
pre-9.12 data-plane saga whose behavior is unchanged.

currentStep.description: Steps advanced so far; advanced by one per tick until it reaches total_steps.

totalSteps.description: Total forward steps in this workflow (bounded; see MAX_WORKFLOW_STEPS).

payload.description:
Opaque JSON payload carried verbatim with every fired transition event; the
consumer interprets it. The workflow tick never executes it in-process.

compensations.description:
Reverse-order compensation payloads handed to the saga engine; the EXISTING
SagaRecoveryWorker dispatches these (reverse-order) when the workflow is
cancelled. Matches `runtime::saga_compensators::CompensationPayload`.

sagaId.description:
The saga row this workflow recorded in `udb_sagas` (the reused engine record).
Cancellation flips this saga into the recoverable state so the existing
recovery worker runs its compensations.

pendingSignal.description: When WAITING_SIGNAL, the signal name the workflow is blocked on.

nextRunAt.description: When the workflow is next eligible to advance. NULL once terminal.

v1WorkflowInstance.description:
WorkflowInstance — a durable, tenant-scoped multi-step operation orchestrated by
the native WorkflowService (master-plan 9.12). The instance is the durable state
that survives a broker restart or leader change: it carries the workflow_type
discriminator, the current/total step counters, the opaque payload, the
reverse-order compensation list, and a link to the saga row the EXISTING saga
engine recorded for it. Forward progress is driven by the leader-elected workflow
tick (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, one advancer cluster-wide); cancellation hands the
linked saga to the existing `SagaRecoveryWorker` so compensation reuses the
established reverse-order machinery rather than reimplementing it.

v1WorkflowStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a durable workflow instance (master-plan 9.12). Only RUNNING
instances whose next_run_at is due are claimed by the leader-elected workflow
tick; terminal states (COMPLETED / COMPENSATED / CANCELLED / FAILED) are never
re-advanced. COMPENSATING is the transitional state while the EXISTING saga
recovery worker reverses the recorded compensations (reverse-order).

 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_PENDING: Recorded but not yet eligible to advance.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_RUNNING: Eligible to advance when next_run_at is due.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_WAITING_SIGNAL: Blocked on an external signal (SignalWorkflow resumes it).
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_COMPLETED: All steps advanced; terminal success.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_COMPENSATING: Cancellation requested; the saga compensation path is undoing side effects.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_COMPENSATED: Compensation completed; terminal.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_CANCELLED: Cancelled by an operator; terminal.
 - WORKFLOW_STATUS_FAILED: Forward execution failed; terminal.
